dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Diabetic striatopathy (non-ketotic hyperglycemia-induced chorea/ballism / chorea–hyperglycaemia–basal ganglia syndrome) due to severe uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, likely precipitated by urinary tract infection.

1. Sydenham chorea (post-streptococcal) – recent pharyngitis reported; ASO titres and throat swab could not be performed, and bilateral striatal MRI signal change would be atypical.
2. Japanese encephalitis or other viral encephalitis with bilateral basal ganglia involvement – less consistent with the T1-hyperintense, T2-hypointense pattern and absence of encephalopathy.
3. Subacute haemorrhage or cavernous malformation in the striatum – would usually be unilateral and show expected blood-product signal; worth revisiting imaging if presentation evolves.
